buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 50% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 50 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 50 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 50 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Service & Support

1. MINIMUM SERVICE CHARGES The minimum service charges shall be 3.85%. Accordingly, the minimum floor price of the tender has bee n calculated considering service charges of 3.85%. Bids quoting service charges of less than 3.85% shall n ot be considered. 2. PENALTY CLAUSE Penal action against any firm defaulting in the timely and legitimate payment of salaries shall be taken in accordance with Paragraph 2.2 of the Manual for Procurement of Consultancy and Other Services, June 202 2, and the applicable provisions of DPM 09. Such action may include debarment or removal from the list of approved firms for a period of up to two years, subject to applicable rules. 3. DISQUALIFICATION OF BIDDER The Seller/Bidder may be disqualified during the technical evaluation stage on the recommendation of the duly constituted Board if found to be a problem creator or a habitual defaulter in any matter involving the present Unit/Headquarters. 4. REGISTERED LOCAL OFFICE The participating firm's main office (Head Office) shall be located in the consignee's city to ensure uninterr upted coordination of services and timely resolution of issues arising during contract execution. The servic e provider shall submit documentary proof of the office address, along with the landline/mobile number of the authorised contact person. Failure to submit the required documents may result in rejection of the bid during technical evaluation.

5. PROTECTION AGAINST FIRM DEFAULT/PENALTY CLAUSE (a) In accordance with the applicable provisions of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 197 0, where the contractor fails to pay wages within the prescribed period or makes short payment, the Princi pal Employer (Buyer) shall discharge the applicable statutory obligations regarding payment of wages to th e contract labour. Any amount paid on behalf of the contractor shall be recovered from the contractor in a ccordance with applicable law. (b) Penal action against any firm defaulting in the timely and legitimate payment of salaries shall be taken in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Manual for Procurement of Consultancy and Other Servi ces, June 2022, and DPM 09. Such action may include debarment or removal from the list of approved firm s for a period of up to two years, subject to applicable rules. 6. PSARA LICENCE Where the manpower to be deployed comprises security guards, the Bidder shall submit a valid licence un der the Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005 (PSARA), as applicable. Failure to submit the requ ired licence shall render the bid liable for rejection during technical evaluation. 7. FINANCIAL SOLVENCY The Bidder shall not be bankrupt or insolvent. Documentary evidence establishing its financial standing sh all be submitted. A self-declaration alone shall not be accepted as sufficient documentary evidence for this requirement. 8. CONDITIONS FOR FORFEITURE OF PERFORMANCE BANK GUARANTEE (PBG) Subject to the terms of the contract and applicable procurement rules, the following defaults may result in forfeiture/invocation of the contractor's PBG, after following the prescribed procedure: (i) Non-compliance with the applicable Minimum Wages Act and the prescribed minimum wage rates. The c ontractor shall ensure payment of wages equal to or higher than the applicable minimum wages. (ii) Failure to pay workers within the prescribed time, and in any event no later than the 7th day of the suc ceeding month, where applicable under the relevant provisions. 9. MULTIPLE L-1 BIDDERS In the event of multiple L-1 bidders, the Run L-1 option shall be exercised in accordance with the applicabl e GeM provisions and procedures. 10. COMPLIANCE WITH BID DOCUMENTS The Bidder shall comply with all requirements, specifications, declarations, certificates and other documen ts stipulated in the bid. 11. EXPERIENCE The firm should have experience in executing similar work for Defence Organisations in Hyderabad/Telang ana. MSEs and start-up firms shall also meet the applicable experience requirements stipulated in the bid, subject to the exemptions, if any, permitted under prevailing Government procurement policies and GeM p rovisions. 12. PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE The successful Bidder shall furnish a Performance Bank Guarantee or other permitted performance securit y instrument equivalent to 5% of the total contract value, in the prescribed format and through an eligible bank, in accordance with the applicable GeM terms and conditions and the timelines stipulated in the bid. 13. PAYING AUTHORITY No advance payment shall be made. Payment shall be processed on a monthly basis after completion of t he relevant services/work and submission and verification of the required supporting documents, through CDA (N), Visakhapatnam, subject to applicable payment procedures. 14. UNSATISFACTORY PERFORMANCE The performance of the contractor under ongoing contracts shall be evaluated by the competent authority . Unsatisfactory performance and failure to comply with contractual terms and conditions may result in act

ion under the applicable contract provisions and procurement rules. Firms issued warning letters for contractual non-compliance may be considered for appropriate action in f uture tenders, subject to applicable rules. Repeated defaults may lead to invocation of PBG and/or short cl osure or termination of the contract, as applicable, after following the prescribed procedure. 15. FINANCIAL POSITION The firm shall maintain sufficient financial resources to continue providing services for a minimum period o f three months, even where payment of bills is delayed due to incomplete or incorrect documentation sub mitted by the service provider or other unforeseen circumstances. 16. SUBMISSION OF CERTIFICATES The Bidder shall duly complete the certificates and declarations specified in the ATC and upload them alon g with the other bid documents for technical evaluation. Failure to submit the required documents may res ult in rejection of the bid, subject to the applicable procurement rules. 17. RESPONSE TO TECHNICAL QUERIES The Bidder shall respond to queries relating to its technical bid within the time specified by the Buyer. Fail ure to respond within the stipulated time may result in rejection of the bid, in accordance with the applicab le procurement rules. 18. SUBMISSION OF ESCALATION MATRIX The Bidder shall submit an escalation matrix for service support in the format specified in the bid, along wi th the other required technical documents. 19. BID SECURING DECLARATION Where applicable under the bid conditions and GeM provisions, the Bidder shall submit a duly signed Bid S ecuring Declaration on the firm's letterhead in the prescribed format. The declaration shall cover the consequences of withdrawal or modification of the bid during its validity per iod and failure by the successful Bidder to sign the contract or submit the required performance security w ithin the stipulated time, as specified in the applicable bidding documents and procurement rules. 20. NON-DISCLOSURE DECLARATION CERTIFICATE The Bidder shall submit a duly signed Non-Disclosure Declaration Certificate in the prescribed format provi ded with the bid, along with the other required documents. 21. GST REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE The firm shall submit a valid GST Registration Certificate, wherever applicable. Failure to submit the requir ed certificate may render the bid liable for rejection. 22. VENDOR REGISTRATION AND BANK DETAILS The Bidder shall possess the required vendor code, wherever applicable, and submit the following docume nts for registration and payment purposes: (a) PAN Card. (b) GSTIN details, wherever applicable. (c) Cancelled cheque. (d) NEFT mandate duly certified by the bank, wherever required. 23. BUYER'S RIGHT TO CANCEL THE BID The Buyer reserves the right to cancel the bid in accordance with applicable GeM provisions and procurem ent rules, without prejudice to any other rights available under the law. 24. SETTLEMENT OF DISPUTES Any dispute arising out of or in connection with the contract shall be dealt with in accordance with the disp

ute resolution provisions of the contract and applicable laws. 25. ACCIDENTS AND CASUALTIES In the event of any accident, mishap or casualty involving the contractor's personnel during the execution of work, the contractor shall comply with all applicable statutory obligations and contractual requirements. Liability shall be determined in accordance with applicable law and the terms of the contract. 26. LABOUR REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE The firm shall submit a valid Labour Registration Certificate, wherever applicable, along with its technical b id. 27. EPF AND ESI REGISTRATION The firm shall submit valid Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees' State Insurance (ESI) registra tion certificates, wherever applicable. 28. SUBMISSION OF PERFORMANCE BANK GUARANTEE The successful Bidder (L-1 firm) shall submit the Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG) within 30 days of the award of the contract, or within the period stipulated in the GeM contract and applicable procurement prov isions, whichever is applicable. 29. ACTS APPLICABLE TO CONTRACTORS The contractor shall comply with all applicable labour laws, rules and statutory provisions relating to the pa yment of wages, minimum wages, employee compensation, industrial disputes, provident fund, maternity benefits, employees' state insurance, gratuity, bonus, child labour and other employment-related matters, as amended from time to time. Such compliance shall include the applicable provisions of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936; Minimum Wag es Act, 1948; Employees' Compensation Act, 1923; Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970; I ndustrial Disputes Act, 1947; Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952; Maternit y Benefit Act, 1961; Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948; Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972; Payment of Bon us Act, 1965; Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986; and other applicable ena ctments, as amended or replaced from time to time. 30. SAFETY EQUIPMENT The contractor shall provide the necessary safety equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), incl uding protective clothing, helmets, goggles, raincoats and other equipment required to protect employees from injury or infection. The contractor shall ensure the proper use of such equipment by its employees. All arrangements shall be made at the contractor's own expense, without additional financial liability to the Government of India/Indi an Navy. Failure to provide the required safety equipment or ensure its proper use may attract a penalty of Rs. 50 f or each established instance of default, subject to the applicable contract provisions. Where prescribed, th e amount shall be deposited with the Government of India through a Military Receivable Order (MRO) withi n four working days of notification of the default. 31. MEDICAL TREATMENT The contractor shall comply with the applicable sanitary and health requirements of the local medical and health authorities. If any employee sustains a major or minor injury within the premises of the establishment during the exec ution of work or in the course of duty, the contractor shall arrange transportation to the nearest appropriat e hospital and provide the required treatment at its own expense, subject to applicable law and contractua l obligations. First aid may be provided by the establishment, as feasible. 32. REPORTING OF ACCIDENTS/INCIDENTS Any accident or incident involving an employee of the contractor within the premises of the establishment

shall be reported immediately by the contractor to the Contract Operating Authority through the Fastest A vailable Means (FAM). 33. SECURITY PROVISIONS The contractor and its employees shall comply with all security instructions and orders issued by the comp etent authority from time to time. They shall also comply with the applicable provisions of the Official Secr ets Act, 1923, as amended from time to time. 34. WAGES AND ALLOWANCES The contractor shall pay salaries/wages to its employees deployed at the establishment from its own resou rces and subsequently submit claims to the Buyer along with the required statutory documents. Such documents shall include proof of remittance of Provident Fund contributions, wage slips and bank sta tements evidencing payment of salaries/wages to the respective employees' bank accounts, as applicable. Wages and allowances shall be paid in accordance with the applicable statutory provisions and the minimu m wages prescribed by the competent Central Government, State Government or other competent authori ty, as applicable. The contractor shall ensure compliance with periodic revisions to the prescribed minimu m wages. Payment of wages for a given month shall be made within the legally prescribed period and, where applica ble, no later than the first week of the following month. The financial liability of the Government of India/Indian Navy shall be limited to the financial implications of the contract, subject to applicable law. 35. NON-ADHERENCE TO PAYMENT TERMS Failure by the contractor to pay wages and allowances to contractual employees within the prescribed peri od shall constitute a breach of contract. The Buyer may take appropriate action, including invocation of the PBG, arranging payment to affected employees where legally permissible, and termination of the contract, in accordance with the contract and applicable law. Continued failure to fulfil contractual obligations may result in further action under applicable procuremen t rules. 36. LEVY OF ADDITIONAL CHARGES All charges levied by the contractor in connection with the services, including placement charges, administ rative charges, bonus-related charges, stationery charges, uniform charges, employee-hiring charges, emp loyee-retention charges, managerial charges, fees, commissions and other similar charges, shall be clearly disclosed and included in the quoted bid price wherever applicable. No unauthorised or undisclosed charges shall be deducted from employees' wages/salaries. The contracto r shall comply with applicable labour laws and the financial terms of the contract. The financial liability of t he Government of India/Indian Navy shall remain limited to the contractual amount, subject to applicable l aw. 37. INSPECTION The Contract Operating Authority and/or its authorised representative may inspect the contractor's compli ance with the contractual provisions at any time during the currency of the contract. Such inspection may form part of the performance evaluation process for assessing service quality, deliver y, commitment and compliance with safety standards. Non-compliance may attract penalties, liquidated d amages or other contractual action, as determined by the competent authority in accordance with the con tract and applicable rules. 38. EMPLOYMENT Employment under this contract shall be contractual. Employees shall not acquire any right to permanent employment with the Government of India/Indian Navy merely on the grounds of continued service under t his contract. The contractor shall remain responsible for its employees and their terms and conditions of employment in accordance with applicable labour laws. The liability of the Government of India/Indian Navy shall be deter

mined in accordance with applicable law and the terms of the contract. 39. DEFINITIONS (a) Contractor: The term "Contractor" means any individual, firm or company, whether incorporated or not , undertaking the contract, including its lawful successors and permitted assigns, as applicable. (b) Employee: The terms "Employee", "Labour", "Worker" and "Workpeople" mean personnel employed by the contractor on a part-time or full-time basis for the execution of this contract. 40. RISK AND EXPENSE CLAUSE (a) If the services, or any instalment thereof, are not delivered within the stipulated period or do not confor m to the contractual requirements, the Buyer may, after allowing the Seller 45 days to remedy the breach where applicable, cancel the contract wholly or partially and exercise other remedies available under the c ontract and applicable law. (b) If the services fail to meet the specifications or parameters stipulated in the contract during the prescri bed inspection or tests, the Buyer may exercise the remedies available under the contract, including cance llation of the contract wholly or partially, as applicable. (c) If a breach relating to the services remains unremedied after the stipulated period, the Buyer may, subj ect to the contract and applicable procurement rules, procure the required services from another source t o remedy the default. (d) Any recoverable excess expenditure incurred in procuring replacement services may be recovered fro m the Seller in accordance with the contract and applicable law. 41. OPTION CLAUSE AND REPEAT ORDER CLAUSE (a) Repeat Order Clause: The Repeat Order Clause shall be exercised only where permitted under the appl icable procurement rules and where incorporated into the bid/contract. The aggregate additional quantity shall remain within the limits prescribed by the applicable procurement provisions. (b) Option Clause: Where the Option Clause is incorporated into the contract, the Purchaser may order add itional quantities up to the limit specified in the contract, at the same rates and on the same terms and con ditions, subject to the applicable procurement rules and the validity period of the clause. 42. FALL CLAUSE Where a Fall Clause is applicable and has been incorporated into the contract, the Seller shall comply with i ts terms and conditions as specified in the contract and the applicable procurement provisions. The Seller shall notify the Buyer of any reduction in the applicable prices of identical services offered to ot her eligible purchasers, wherever required under the contract. Where prescribed, the Seller shall furnish the required price-compliance certificate along with each bill sub mitted for payment. 43. FORCE MAJEURE CLAUSE (a) Neither party shall be held responsible for failure to perform its contractual obligations to the extent th at such failure results from Force Majeure circumstances beyond its reasonable control, subject to the ter ms of the contract and applicable law. (b) The time for performance of the affected obligations may be extended for the period during which the Force Majeure circumstances continue, subject to the contract. (c) The affected party shall notify the other party in writing of the commencement and cessation of the For ce Majeure circumstances within the period stipulated in the contract. (d) Supporting documentary evidence from a competent authority may be required to establish the occurr ence and duration of the Force Majeure circumstances. (e) If the Force Majeure circumstances continue beyond the period stipulated in the contract, either party may exercise its rights under the applicable termination provisions, subject to the contractual terms and a pplicable law. 44. BUYER'S RIGHT TO CANCEL THE BID

The Buyer reserves the right to cancel the bid in accordance with applicable GeM provisions and procurem ent rules, without prejudice to any other rights available under the law. 45. SETTLEMENT OF DISPUTES Any dispute arising out of or in connection with the contract shall be resolved in accordance with the dispu te resolution provisions of the contract and applicable laws. 46. RETENTION OF EXISTING RESOURCES The contractor shall retain the existing trained resources under the contract, as specified in the bid and su bject to applicable eligibility requirements. The Buyer shall provide the requisite documentation and details relating to EPF, ESIC and other applicable statutory requirements necessary for onboarding the retained resources with the new service provider, wh erever required. Police verification of retained resources, where required, shall be carried out by the authority responsible u nder the contract and applicable rules. The new service provider shall not charge retained resources any amount for onboarding them onto its pa yroll. Replacement of resources, where required, shall be undertaken in accordance with the contract and applicable procedures. 47. LABOUR COMMISSIONER CORRESPONDENCE The contractor shall be responsible for handling and responding to correspondence from the Labour Comm issioner relating to its employees and statutory obligations during and after the conclusion of the contract, wherever applicable. 48. TERMINATION FOLLOWING REPEATED WARNINGS Where a third warning letter is issued to the contractor, the contractor shall submit its reply within the peri od specified in the notice, which shall not exceed one month from the date of issuance of the third warning letter. Failure to submit a reply within the stipulated period may result in further contractual action, includi ng termination, in accordance with the contract and applicable procurement rules. . 8. Buyer Added Bid Specific SLA Text Clause(s) The Bidder shall upload the following valid documents along with the bid for technical evaluation: 1. Local Office Address Proof: Documentary proof of the firm's local office at the consignee's locatio n, along with valid contact details. 2. Labour Licence: A valid Labour Licence/Registration Certificate, wherever applicable under the rel evant laws. 3. Past Experience: Documentary proof of experience in providing similar services to Government D epartments, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), or other organisations. Acceptable documents may include GeM Work Orders, Contract Performance Reports (CRACs), or other relevant work orders. 4. Turnover Documents: CA-certified turnover statements for each of the last three financial years, with the turnover for each financial year clearly indicated. 5. GST Registration Certificate: A valid GST Registration Certificate, wherever applicable. 6. MSME/Startup Certificate: A valid Udyam Registration Certificate for MSEs or a recognised Startu p Certificate, wherever applicable. 7. Other Relevant Documents: Any other certificates, declarations or supporting documents specifi cally required under the bid terms and conditions.
